items.headline: 2 new proven top-timers in 90 days
items.detail: Wallet(s) that just crossed the ROI+capital bar by selling a top at profit — a burst means distribution is starting.

items.headline: Holders ~25% underwater — and still not selling
items.detail: MVRV 0.75: price is 25% below the crowd's avg on-chain cost basis ($0.478). Yet 55% of supply is in the longest-held tier — the float isn't moving.
items.framing: Maximum financial pain, minimal capitulation — conviction being tested and, so far, holding.
items.note: Describe the divergence, NOT a bottom call. "Not selling", not "buy".

items.headline: -84% below its all-time high
items.detail: Deepest drawdown on record was -95%; it has made new highs after every prior one so far.
items.framing: Deep drawdowns are the toll — it's paid them before (no recovery promise).
items.note: It's deep and unrecovered NOW; don't imply it always recovers.

items.headline: SPX's MVRV 0.75 = 2th percentile of Bitcoin's history
items.detail: SPX's MVRV of 0.75 sits at the 2th percentile of Bitcoin's entire MVRV history — as cheap as BTC's generational bottoms.
items.framing: MVRV is unitless, so it's comparable: SPX today is at BTC's 2th percentile. BTC was only this cheap at major bottoms.
items.note: A position on BTC's map, not a date-match forecast.

items.headline: 80% of all-time holders are gone — 92% of today's never sold to zero
items.detail: Of 27,209 wallets that ever held ≥5k SPX, 5,376 remain (80% churned). Yet 92% of CURRENT holders have never once sold to zero — survivorship.
items.framing: Enormous all-time churn, but the survivors are diamond-handed. The honest "who's still here" read.
items.note: Right-censoring: recent cohorts read high. "Gone" = fell below the 5k bar.

items.headline: NUPL -0.33 — capitulation
items.detail: Net unrealised profit/loss is -0.33 (from MVRV 0.75) — the market sits in the capitulation zone.
items.framing: Aggregate holder profitability. Below zero = the crowd is underwater, historically an accumulation zone.
items.note: A position read, not a signal.

items.headline: Smart money still net-selling (-19.6% over 12w)
items.detail: The 9-wallet cohort of proven top-timers (ROI ≥5×, still holding) holds 5.65M SPX. 4w -2.1% · 12w -19.6% · 26w -25%.
items.framing: Smart money hasn't started buying yet (-19.6% in 12w). Honest "not the bottom signal yet" read.
items.checkable: A recomputed cohort of wallets with realized ROI ≥5× that still hold ≥50k SPX; net flow of their combined balance.

items.headline: 5.78M SPX pulled off exchanges in 7 days
items.detail: Net exchange balance change is 1.4σ from its trailing norm — coins leaving to self-custody (supply tightening).
items.framing: SPX is leaving exchanges — 5.78M in a week, above the usual. Frame as coins moving to self-custody / supply tightening, not a guaranteed pump.
items.checkable: Net exchange balance from the tagged CEX wallets, over the public transfer history.

items.headline: -1.2σ below its trend vs the alt market
items.detail: SPX ÷ the alt sector (ex-BTC/ETH/stables), detrended, sits 1.2σ below its own trend — cheap vs alts.
items.framing: Relative value vs the whole alt sector — -1.2σ cheap. SPX structurally outperforms alts, so this is deviation from ITS trend, not parity.
items.note: A relative-value position, not a signal.

items.headline: SOPR 0.885 — coins moving at a loss
items.detail: Spent-output profit ratio is 0.885: coins that moved on-chain realised a loss on average. Sustained <1 = capitulation, >1 = profit-taking.
items.framing: On-chain realised behaviour — loss-realisation (SOPR 0.885).
items.note: Only coins that MOVED; a behaviour read, not a signal.
